instructions: Up to 4 days ahead, heat the oven to 350°F. Brush the vegetable oil into all 12 cups of a muffin pan.
Peel the 3 bananas and break them into a blender.
Add the 2 cups oats, 2 eggs, 1/4 cup milk, 1/4 cup maple syrup, 1 tsp baking soda and 1 tsp vanilla. Blend until it's mostly smooth, with a few small bits of oat left.
Add the 1/3 cup chocolate chips and pulse for a few seconds to mix them in.
Divide the batter between the 12 cups.
Bake for 15 to 17 minutes, until a skewer in the middle of one comes out clean. This makes 12 muffins.
Cool them in the pan for 10 minutes, then lift them onto a rack to cool completely.

They keep in the fridge for up to 4 days in a sealed container, or in the freezer for up to 3 months. In the morning, eat one at room temperature or microwave it for about 20 seconds. Thaw frozen ones on the counter for 30 to 60 minutes first.
advance_prep_notes: Bake the muffins up to 4 days ahead and keep them in the fridge.
method_notes: All three are built on ripe bananas and rolled oats. Kristine's Kitchen (the lead) blends whole oats, bananas, eggs, a little milk and maple syrup in a blender with no flour, then pulses in mini chocolate chips and bakes them at 350°F. Well Plated blends oats with Greek yogurt and honey and bakes them hotter, and Ambitious Kitchen's vegan version stirs oats into a flour batter with flax and coconut oil. This one follows the lead's 12 muffins, with any milk in place of almond milk.
